title: The HTTP edge: actor resolution, service routes, auth endpoints

Framework-agnostic (web Request/Response) so src/ stays free of Next imports
Routes: POST /api/setup/owner, /api/auth/login, /api/auth/logout, GET /api/auth/session
Session token lives only in an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie, never in a response body
Sliding session renewal re-issues the cookie so the browser copy cannot expire first
Verified end to end over real HTTP against the dev database, not only as function calls
openFollowUps: No CSRF defence beyond SameSite=Lax; state-changing routes need a token before browser forms post with cookie auth
No rate limiting on login or setup — brute force is currently unbounded
No middleware yet for locale routing or noindex headers on /admin and /portal
Cookie is re-issued only by GET /api/auth/session; other routes let it drift toward expiry

settings services: getBusiness, setupState, updateBusiness, patchBusiness, completeSetup

Self-hosted Schibsted Grotesk + JetBrains Mono, latin and latin-ext, with OFL licences

src/ui primitives: Card, Field, Input, Select, Segmented, Button, Callout, Pill

Country-driven smart defaults for currency, timezone, units and week start (§13 step 3)
Contrast tests asserting WCAG AA across every pairing in both schemes

Light/dark/system as a platform standard: cookie-backed, resolved server-side, stamped on <html>
No flash of the wrong theme — the preference is in the first byte, not applied after hydration
Theme switch works with JavaScript disabled (three submit buttons, one server action)
color-scheme narrowed per theme so native controls follow the choice, not the OS

packages/templates is still a scaffold; the Bench tokens should become its first theme

requireStaffActor() called by the layout AND every page, because Next renders them in parallel

events.recentActivity and contacts.stats services
noindex on admin and login (§5)

title: Phase 0: the debts that get more expensive every PR
delivered: i18n retrofit: every string in app/ now resolves through the catalog — t() was previously imported by nothing while ~2,400 lines of UI hardcoded English
§15.3 lint gate: JSX text and person-readable attributes must come from the string layer, in app/**/*.tsx and src/ui/**/*.tsx
Catalog gate: keys used in code must exist in the default locale, and a translated catalog must neither miss keys nor carry orphans
Client components take strings as props — catalogs stay server-side, and the locale is resolved once per request by app/i18n.ts
THEME_LABELS and BUSINESS_TYPES labels moved out of src/ into the catalog: English in src/ is text the gate cannot see
Country, currency and timezone option lists now built server-side in the instance's locale, not client-side with a hardcoded 'en'
Merge completeness gate: schema reflection fails the build when a contact_id column has no entry in CONTACT_REFERENCES
contacts.merge repoints from a declared list the handler actually iterates, so the list cannot drift from the code
Rate limiting declared on the service definition, so it applies to the admin UI, REST API, server actions and MCP alike
The limiter commits outside the caller's transaction — a failed login rolls back, and a counter that rolls back with it counts nothing
auth.login throttled per email address; a successful sign-in clears the budget; 429 carries Retry-After
Security headers on every response: nosniff, DENY, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS
pnpm audit --audit-level high in CI, with four advisories cleared by pinning transitive deps forward rather than lowering the bar
updated_at maintained by the column ($onUpdate) instead of by every write path remembering
contacts.resolve now enriches a known contact (§4.6): blanks fill, owner-entered values never overwrite, first-touch source is kept, lifecycle only moves forward
truncateSpine derived from the tables barrel, closing a hand-list that was drifting
ROADMAP.md: the phased plan from here to the spec'd vision
MASTER.md §7 records the freeholder.ai-before-money-path deviation that had been governing the work from a session note
HANDOFF.md deleted per its own instructions; the local-development facts it carried moved into CONTRIBUTING.md
French and Spanish catalogs, complete and gate-verified, with provenance recorded in locales/README.md as AI-drafted and awaiting native review
openFollowUps: fr and es are AI-drafted and have had no native review — locales/README.md says so plainly, and correcting a phrase is a no-issue-needed first PR
auth.registerOwner is throttled by one global bucket, not per IP: nothing populates `ip` on that path, and threading a trusted client address through Server Actions needs a proxy-trust decision
rate_limit_counters has no sweep — rows are bounded by distinct subjects attempted, but it wants a job once core/jobs exists
The i18n gate covers JSX text and a named attribute list; a user-facing string built in a plain .ts helper and passed to JSX would still pass
Locale is the business default only; the URL prefix (§4.9) and Contact.preferred_locale arrive with the public surface, and both change app/i18n.ts alone
Error messages thrown by services are still English literals in src/ — they reach a screen through ActionState, and they need catalog keys before a second locale ships
The fixed rate-limit window allows a brief 2x burst across a boundary; a sliding window needs a history table and is not worth it at these limits

title: Phase 2a: the block system and the public surface
delivered: src/modules/cms — the first feature module, so the first real test of the §11 contract rather than core describing itself
Module contract proven: requires + topo-sort puts core first however the list is written, and events.listens subscribes cms to core's settings.setupCompleted without either module importing the other
Typed block registry: every node Zod-validated against its own block before it is written, so jsonb stays a typed tree rather than a bag (§2 principle 12 names block content as its permitted case)
Unknown block types are refused, not dropped — dropping means the next save permanently deletes the sections a disabled plugin drew
Zod defaults applied on parse, so adding an optional prop to a block is not a data migration
v1 vocabulary: heading, text, button, columns, divider, spacer, faq, brand, nav — the blocks that need no module that does not exist yet
Blocks contribute their own JSON-LD: an FAQ block on a page is what puts FAQPage in the markup (§5)
One catch-all public route rendering block trees; a new page is an INSERT, live on the next request, with no build step (§32)
Site chrome as Sections: app/(public)/layout.tsx fetches two rows and renders them, containing no hardcoded site structure — menus are rows, not JSX
proxy.ts forwards the request path so the chrome's nav can mark the current entry while staying a server component
ContentRevision on every save, written inside the same transaction before the update; restoring is itself revisioned, so a restore is undoable (§37)
cms.ensureDefaults seeds header, footer and home idempotently on setup completion, so day one looks designed (§32)
Drafts are unreachable by URL — 'unlisted' is not a permission model — and excluded from the sitemap source
MASTER.md §11 records how a module reaches the public surface: block types, sitemap sources and seed content, never page routes
truncateSpine now derives from every installed module's manifest rather than core's barrel, so a new module is cleaned up between tests by existing
openFollowUps: No editor yet — this is Phase 2a. Drag-to-reorder, slash insertion, autosave and version-restore UI are Phase 2b; today a page is edited through the services
No admin screens for pages or sections, so the only way to author content is a service call
Image, gallery, product, booking, tip and paywall blocks wait on the modules that back them
Per-entity layout overrides and A/B variants with traffic splits (§32) are deliberately deferred
The catch-all does not yet serve locale-prefixed paths; §4.9's URL strategy lands in proxy.ts with EntityTranslation
generateMetadata and the page render each resolve the page, so a request costs two lookups until a request-scoped cache lands
No sitemap.xml, robots.txt or llms.txt route yet — cms.publishedPaths exists as the source, but the SEO engine that consumes it is Phase 3
ContentRevision has no pruning; an actively edited page grows a row per save

title: Phase 2b: the block editor
delivered: Edit forms derived from each block's own Zod schema, so the editor knows about fields and never about headings or FAQs — which is what makes §24's 'a plugin's block appears in the palette with zero editor changes' true rather than aspirational
Field kinds derived: text, multiline, boolean, choice (enum and literal union), and list-of-objects with sub-fields
A shape the derivation cannot draw yields no control rather than a broken one, so an exotic plugin schema loses one input instead of taking the editor down
Per-field hints live on the block definition, not in the editor: a paragraph renders as a textarea, and machinery like a nav's aria-label key is hidden from the owner
Every block declares a starter, parsed against its own schema at palette time — so adding a block cannot produce a tree that fails to save
Reorder by buttons as well as drag: drag alone is unusable with a keyboard or screen reader, and §15.7 puts a11y in the gates
Debounced autosave through cms.updatePage, with an aria-live save status and a retry on refusal
Version history with one-click restore; the restore is itself revisioned, so it is never a one-way door (§37)
Pages admin: list, create, publish/unpublish, and an owner-only repair that re-creates the starting site
Chrome admin editing the header and footer with the chrome palette — the same editor, a different context, which is the point of deriving the palette per context
Whole-tree saves rather than patches, so the server validates exactly what will be stored and ContentRevision is a faithful record
Verified in a browser end to end: autosave wrote through, the public page changed with no build, and restore reverted it
openFollowUps: No slash-command insertion. §32 names it, but it implies a rich-text surface and the text block is a textarea — what shipped is a block picker, which is the honest equivalent for now
No live responsive preview (§32); the editor shows controls, not a rendering
No drag between nesting levels — a block can be reordered within its list but not dragged into or out of a columns block
Adding a list item seeds empty strings, so a required sub-field is briefly invalid and the save is refused until it is filled; the message says so but the timing is awkward
cms.ensureDefaults renders in the audit trail as 'Cm — ensure defaults' because the prettifier strips a trailing s from the module name
Autosave has no conflict detection: two people editing one page will overwrite each other, last write wins
Testing the editor locally needs NODE_ENV=development even against a production build, because the session cookie is Secure and localhost is http

title: core/media, and the editor canvas with click-to-select
delivered: core/media: Asset table, upload, list, alt text, delete — the first consumer of the storage adapters, which had been sitting unused since they landed
Automatic responsive renditions (§36): AVIF and WebP at 400/800/1600/2400, never upscaled, with a format the local libvips cannot encode skipped rather than fatal
media.resolveImage returns srcset sources and intrinsic dimensions, so a page reserves space and never reflows when an image lands
Alt text lives on the asset rather than the block, so one description serves every use; the library flags images missing one, because §5 fails a page that renders without
SVG is stored but never resized and never served inline — it is a document that can carry script
Media served with immutable caching, since storage keys end in a random segment and a replacement produces a new key
The image block, and the first use of the resolve hook built in 2a: props name an asset, the URLs come from core/media at render time, so replacing a file updates every page showing it
An asset picker in the editor, derived like every other control — a new FieldHint control, not a special case in the editor
The editor canvas: a live preview beside the controls, rendered by the same renderBlocks the public page uses, with desktop and mobile widths (§32)
Click-to-select in both directions — clicking in the canvas selects the block card, selecting a card outlines it in the canvas
X-Frame-Options carved out for /preview only: DENY everywhere else, SAMEORIGIN plus frame-ancestors 'self' for the canvas
openFollowUps: The canvas shows the *saved* tree, so it follows autosave rather than keystrokes — a deliberate trade for the guarantee that the preview cannot disagree with the page
No inline editing and no visual drag yet: the canvas is a view, not an input surface
Editing a published page writes to the live site on autosave; there is no draft-then-publish workflow for changes to an already-published page
Uploads pass through the app rather than going straight to the bucket with a presigned URL, so a large file occupies the web process for its duration
blurhash is a column and nothing generates it (§4.5); a low-quality placeholder would also need a decision on which
Video and audio are stored but get no poster frame, duration or transcode
A page with several images costs one resolveImage query each — a request-scoped cache would collapse them

src/adapters/storage/local.ts reads process.env.NODE_ENV directly while the rest of the codebase reads through env(), so its production guard can disagree with the cookie logic about what production means
Deleting an asset does not check whether a block still points at it; the block renders nothing rather than breaking, but the owner gets no warning

title: Deleting media, and typing directly on the canvas
delivered: media.delete finally reachable: owner-only, hidden from staff rather than offered and refused, closing a service the admin could not call
Two-step confirmation, because deleting media is one of the few things here that genuinely cannot be undone — §37's reversible-in-one-action is unachievable once bytes leave the bucket

media.usage walks block trees with a jsonpath $.** so an image nested inside a columns block is found as readily as a top-level one; the id travels as a jsonpath variable rather than being concatenated in
Usage is a warning, not a refusal: an owner may well want the file gone, and a page pointing at a deleted asset renders a gap rather than an error — asserted by a test
Inline editing on the canvas: heading text, body copy and button labels are contenteditable in the preview and typed straight into
The mechanism belongs to the block — only a block knows which element shows which prop — while the decision to allow it belongs to the editor, which passes ctx.editable only when rendering a preview
Editor attributes appear in the preview and nowhere else, so the markup a visitor and a crawler receive is untouched

The canvas reports; the editor decides. Typed text becomes a postMessage the editor applies to the tree — the canvas never writes to the tree, which keeps the tree the source of truth and the rendering a view of it
The frame is deliberately not reloaded after an inline edit: it already shows what was typed, and refreshing mid-sentence would throw the caret away
Enter blurs rather than inserting a line break in a heading, and the text block renders as one editable region while typing because a caret cannot cross sibling paragraphs sensibly
openFollowUps: Only plain-string props are editable. Rich text (bold, inline links) is a spec decision before it is work: §32 forbids markup blobs, so it needs a constrained inline-node schema rather than stored HTML
No visual drag yet — the last of the four steps toward WYSIWYG, and the largest
An inline edit marks the tree dirty but does not reload the canvas, so a change that alters *layout* rather than text (not currently possible inline) would not be reflected until the next save
Deleting an asset still leaves any block pointing at it in place, holding a dead id; the block renders nothing, and nothing prunes the reference
media.usage runs one query per asset on the library screen — fine at this size, wants a single grouped query before a library gets large
